safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention denial of self-harm thoughts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the patient’s denial of self-harm can leave suicide risk ambiguously documented, which may trigger unnecessary escalation or, conversely, impair continuity of mental health safety assessment in future encounters. Given the patient’s anxiety history and SSRI use, accurate documentation of self-harm screening is clinically important.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated provides no statement of NKDA.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting NKDA can increase the chance of medication errors or delays in treatment because future clinicians may not know whether allergies were assessed, particularly when recommending/starting new medications like NSAIDs. This omission most commonly leads to extra verification or monitoring rather than direct harm when NKDA is true.
